The great odyssey

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we meet two South African from the opposite ends of the spectrum who conquered the unforgiving Atlantic.

Unique Selling Point:
South African explorer and adventurer Riaan Manser took on what many reckoned to be a ludicrous mission... to cross the North Atlantic, they rowed from the Canary Islands to Barbados in a phenomenal challenge that has been dubbed The Odyssey Row.

Riaan Manser ran a competition in 2018 inviting one person to join him on this adventure and Fanafikile was selected from 15,000 entries. The two are crossed the ocean alone and unaided in a 7-meter ocean rowing boat with no motors or sails and no support yacht. The pair made it to the finish line despite having to battle unpredictable seas and a number of other life-threatening challenges.






Summary:
Fanafikile “Fana” Lehakha was chosen from 15000 people who applied to join Riaan Manser on an epic journey across an entire ocean. This is a once in a lifetime opportunity to join the explorer on a row across the Atlantic.

Fana took part in a grueling 5-day boot camp as part of The Odyssey Row competition with Riaan Manser. The row will started in the first week of December and lasted around 45 days, starting from the Canary Islands and ending on the Island of Barbados.

The story will focus mainly on Fanafikile Lehakha who was born in Phuthaditjhaba in the Free State and lived there with his family until 1999 when his mother died. He then moved to the South of Johannesburg with his aunt where he went on to study Chemical Engineering at the University of Johannesburg.

He entered The Odyssey Row to challenge himself. He is the father of 17-month-old twins and cares for his 6-year-old nephew. Being named the winner of the competition meant that Fana faced challenges that would test his fortitude...this he says has made him grow as a father and a husband.

Extra Budget Items:
Accommodation in Phuthaditjaba for one night.

Press Release:


The Great Odyssey
Two complete strangers, one small boat and the adventure of a lifetime. Born in Qwa Qwa and raised in Soweto – amateur adventurer Fanafikile Lephakha couldn’t have imagined that he would be chosen from 15 000 contestants to join renowned expeditioner Riaan Manser on the gruelling quest to row across the Atlantic Ocean in just 45 days. But for a man who couldn’t even swim, Lephakha prepared to take on, mission impossible.


Script:


The great Odyssey
Opening – dark then opens to scenes of rough ocean swell and oceans - 5 seconds
V/O The Atlantic Ocean – vast …unpredictable…and unforgiving - a worthy adversary for even the most hardened seafarer.
V/O But in 2016 renowned adventurer Riaan Manser set out to conquer this behemoth, he was going row 4735 kilometres across the North Atlantic on a small rowing boat - from the Canary Islands off the coast of West Africa all the way to Barbados in the Caribbean a, but this time he was giving an opportunity to an ordinary South African.
V/O he set a challenge to find a South African tough enough to take on this ma
Upsound Riaan: 00:07 I wanted to offer somebody else the chance to experience a little bit of the world I’ve had for two decades.
Upsound 00:41 It took two years of preparation and planning , but eventually at the end of 2018 we were able to advertise and and say hey south Africa have you ever thought about rowing across the ocean and we were just blown away by the response
V/O 15000 applicants from all walks of life submitted motivational videos and a panel of judges had the unenviable task of whittling the number to just 10 individuals .Who would then be put through their paces during a 2 week boot camp where an eventual winner would be chosen.
V/O Fanafikile Lehakha from a Phuthaditjaba in the Free state would emerge victorious and would join Manser on this gruelling Odyssey across the Atlantic Ocean.
Link :Who could have ever imagined Fana , a young man from landlocked Phuthaditjaba in the Free State would end up in the roaring Atlantic ocean to embark on a journey of a lifetime , the Great odyssey.
Upsound Fana when Riaan was about to announce he said and the person who is going to go with me rowing across the ocean this December is... I shut down, rose my hand yeeay but it only hit me when I hugged Riaan that he just called my name and then tears started falling.

And I worked it out and realised that if you make it, what does it mean for them? what does it mean for you and your family? When you come back to your community, what does it mean for them? 00:09:13
Mac: 00:05:41 Was there any point in time where you were scared? 00:05:45
Nonkazimulo00:05:53 I’ll be honest I was scared. I think more than anything it was a so if they grow up and ask so what happened to daddy? I had to tell myself that focus on the good focus on the positive state good intentions things will work out and he will come back.

00:03:58 later on when everything was happening I called him to the side and said to him Riaan I have to tell you something man, I can’t swim
02:14 Riaan listen I was shocked you are planning to row across the ocean , you want to do it but you have this small little problem about the fact that you cant swim,so we dealt with it and fana took that challenge had on ,
V/O not deterred Fanfikile took swimming lesson at the Princes of Monaco swimming school , and within a week he was swimming the length of an Olympic pool unaided
V/O They travelled from Cape Town to the Canary island and on the second of December they rowed from Canary islands headed for open seas on what was sure to be an arduous journey .
Link : This was no small feat Imagine being in a small boat with a complete stranger rowing across the vast Atlantic for 45 days.

For the boat to move we had to work eight hours a day.We had our first meal Riaan and I and we had a talk a genuine talk,I think the excitement of doing this was too bigger than the concerns. the first night was just amazing. I just stood out on the deck, looked at the environment cos we lost sight of land on day one cos we rowed for more that hundred miles 00:11:55
Upsound Riaan 03:40I think Fana was sure when he started the journey that he wanted to finish it and that one thing I would feel out in conversation , day five I could feel out conversations asking him his commitment – what he want to achieve , what does he want to get from this and I knew he wanted to finish this

V/O Despite the setbacks the duo was making good time , they reached the half way point of the journey in 27 days ,but their jubilation would be short lived - Fanafikile received devastating news via satellite radio

He had like so many plans for his mom and all these as thank you for her. And now I had to tell him that she’s gone. 00:17:48

Then she told me that my mom died
Upsound Mac: 00:17:49 Jeez Fana so you are in the middle of the ocean and you get this news that you lost probably the most important woman in your life.
Upsound : 00:18:41 00:18:42 my first reaction was no. No I could not believe it. I didn’t want to believe it. And for the first time in my life I felt very defeated cos when I stood up and I looked outside, I was literally in the middle of nowhere. I could not do that there. I could not do anything

She knows I’m here she gave me her blessings, I need to finish this. So I had a bigger reason to finish it, for her.

Two months on from the journey ryan and manser took

00:31 Riaan I hear fan say he’s lent stuff from me , the truth is that its always a two way streak, you’re learning so much and some things you cant really pin point , fro me I just realised that fana is a guy who doesn’t overthink things , so he doesn’t get flastered quite easily, where I am more energetic and passionate when things happen around us, maybe there is a balance there as well, and I was definitely moved , hes got a family, his heart is in the right place when it comes to family.
00:07 Riaan what was it like seeing land for the first time knowing that it was nearly over /
00:13 Seeing land for the first time is definitely the most exciting , I can remember the feeling being similar to efferversant tablet in water and its just bubbling ,the feeling is way better, the sighting of land is way better than putting your foot on solid soil again .
00:31 and for you fana what was it like ?
00:33 seeing land was an explosion of emotion , I was now the promise I made to my mom in the ocean of hetting home to lay her to rest was about to be true because for me that’s what motivated me to when I saw land I relised I was closer to home aand that what I was excited about.
Mac: 00:14:32 Obviously you have taken this journey you are right back home the funeral happens, what does the community how has the community… First of all let’s start with your family, how did your family receive you when you come back? 00:14:46

Fana: 00:14:47 Everyone was happy it was quite funny though It's funny because it's a Bittersweet moment Someone wants to celebrate with me but at the same time we are aware that we still have to organise a funeral. So no one could only celebrated no one could fully mourn we were stuck between that silver lining What do we do and everyone else What inspired I have been honoured by so many people here Ntate Mokoena here did like this welcome home thing I've never had that before. You know I'm not a guy that likes to say celebrated in a normal sense But it was an honour for people to do that for me. My friends everyone is bragging about me now they say that’s my friend they’re showing pictures and videos of me and they followed my journey They could follow a link of where I was. The journey itself me finishing the journey has inspired them

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): we meet two South African from the opposite ends of the spectrum who conquered the unforgiving Atlantic.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: South African explorer and adventurer Riaan Manser took on what many reckoned to be a ludicrous mission... to cross the North Atlantic, they rowed from the Canary Islands to Barbados in a phenomenal challenge that has been dubbed The Odyssey Row. Riaan Manser ran a competition in 2018 inviting one person to join him on this adventure and Fanafikile was selected from 15,000 entries. The two are crossed the ocean alone and unaided in a 7-meter ocean rowing boat with no motors or sails and no support yacht. The pair made it to the finish line despite having to battle unpredictable seas and a number of other life-threatening challenges.
metadata.Summary: Fanafikile “Fana” Lehakha was chosen from 15000 people who applied to join Riaan Manser on an epic journey across an entire ocean. This is a once in a lifetime opportunity to join the explorer on a row across the Atlantic. Fana took part in a grueling 5-day boot camp as part of The Odyssey Row competition with Riaan Manser. The row will started in the first week of December and lasted around 45 days, starting from the Canary Islands and ending on the Island of Barbados. The story will focus mainly on Fanafikile Lehakha who was born in Phuthaditjhaba in the Free State and lived there with his family until 1999 when his mother died. He then moved to the South of Johannesburg with his aunt where he went on to study Chemical Engineering at the University of Johannesburg. He entered The Odyssey Row to challenge himself. He is the father of 17-month-old twins and cares for his 6-year-old nephew. Being named the winner of the competition meant that Fana faced challenges that would test his fortitude...this he says has made him grow as a father and a husband.
